cards.text: Psalm 150 is the very last psalm, and the psalmist opens by calling out to anyone listening: "Hallelujah! Praise God in His sanctuary." No warm-up, friend. The oven's already HOT.

cards.question: In Psalm 150, the call to praise God stays inside His sanctuary and goes nowhere else.

cards.text: Nope, there's more: "Praise Him in His mighty heavens." Friend, I spent YEARS stuck in one drawer, and this psalm won't even stay in ONE place.

cards.question: Psalm 150 has told us where to praise God. Then comes this: "Praise Him for His mighty acts; praise Him for His excellent greatness." What is the psalm telling us now?

cards.text: Then the psalm calls in the band: "Praise Him with the sound of the horn; praise Him with the harp and lyre." Me, I've got one instrument, the oven timer, and it knows exactly ONE song: DING.

cards.question: After the horn, harp and lyre, Psalm 150 pairs the tambourine with something that isn't an instrument at all. That something is dancing.

cards.text: Tambourine AND dancing, then strings and flute. Me dancing on a gold base is just hopping, friend, but it's VERY dignified hopping.

Then come the cymbals: "Praise Him with clashing cymbals; praise Him with resounding cymbals." Years in that junk drawer, the loudest thing I ever heard was a dead battery rolling over, and now the psalm wants CYMBALS, then MORE CYMBALS.

cards.question: Clashing cymbals, then resounding cymbals. As Psalm 150 heads for its finish, the praise is getting ___.
Psalm 150 has called in the whole band. Then it turns to who should praise the LORD. Who does it call?

cards.text: "Let everything that has breath praise the LORD! Hallelujah!" Friend, I'm a stamper on a gold base with no lungs at ALL, and you better believe I'm still waving this mustache.

cards.question: Psalm 150 ends with the same word it starts with.
